provisional_features.title: Bootstrap ledger, PlanUnit, and node-readiness ownership is separated
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: Planning Ledger owns source memory and compilation boundaries, Plan Document owns standardized PlanUnits and indexes, Plan-to-node owns the readiness-only future interface, and Bootstrap Migration owns workflow and seal timing. Ordinary planning cannot mutate governance artifacts.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap preserved: Planning Ledger owns source memory and compilation boundaries, Plan Document owns standardized PlanUnits and indexes, Plan-to-node owns the readiness-only future interface, and Bootstrap Migration owns workflow and seal timing. Ordinary planning cannot mutate governance artifacts.

provisional_features.title: Runtime-capable direction is not runtime enablement
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: The PRD/Planning packet may record runtime-capable v2 contracts, but the current compile cannot launch runtime or emit WorkNodes, queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, build tasks, dispatch, or Orchestrator builds.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap preserved: The PRD/Planning packet may record runtime-capable v2 contracts, but the current compile cannot launch runtime or emit WorkNodes, queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, build tasks, dispatch, or Orchestrator builds.

provisional_features.title: Goal Runtime owner map lacks transition seam oracles
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: The owner map is exceptionally detailed and protects phase boundaries, but no seam oracle defines provider-hook promotion, worker/verifier model changes during a goal, resolution failure, stale settings, or receipt attribution across the listed owners.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Observed provider hook and model transition undefined: The owner map is exceptionally detailed and protects phase boundaries, but no seam oracle defines provider-hook promotion, worker/verifier model changes during a goal, resolution failure, stale settings, or receipt attribution across the listed owners.

provisional_features.title: Plans-to-code handoff remains design-only
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: The handoff map names future runtime owners and metadata outputs while expressly prohibiting PlanCompile enablement, native launch, nodes, queues, implementation files, GoalRuns, build tasks, and dispatch.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap preserved: The handoff map names future runtime owners and metadata outputs while expressly prohibiting PlanCompile enablement, native launch, nodes, queues, implementation files, GoalRuns, build tasks, and dispatch.

provisional_features.title: Forbidden artifact counts are machine-fixed to zero
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: All eight forbidden artifact categories are required and fixed to zero, including WorkNodes, implementation files, runtime launches, and production build tasks.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap preserved: All eight forbidden artifact categories are required and fixed to zero, including WorkNodes, implementation files, runtime launches, and production build tasks.

provisional_features.title: 0PI-001 is retired migration lineage and cannot own product coverage
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: The former source-preserving bridge is accepted only as a compatibility disposition; its live mode is source_preserving_bridge_retired, it creates no WorkNodes, and named fine-grained PlanUnits or explicit dispositions own coverage.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap preserved: The former source-preserving bridge is accepted only as a compatibility disposition; its live mode is source_preserving_bridge_retired, it creates no WorkNodes, and named fine-grained PlanUnits or explicit dispositions own coverage.

provisional_features.title: Readiness inputs lack a common atomic snapshot identity
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, retained as a local catalog conclusion subject to later research and scenario certification: Buildability joins human-updated blockers, generated certification, and node-readiness state, but the matrix defines no shared revision, generation epoch, lock, or snapshot identity across those inputs.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Observed multi artifact snapshot identity missing: Buildability joins human-updated blockers, generated certification, and node-readiness state, but the matrix defines no shared revision, generation epoch, lock, or snapshot identity across those inputs.

provisional_features.title: Open Folder accessible name is unresolved
provisional_features.summary: Validated packet observation, pending independent conclusion testing: The Open Folder control is explicitly inventoried with a missing accessible-name candidate.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Observed accessibility gap: The Open Folder control is explicitly inventoried with a missing accessible-name candidate.

provisional_features.title: Task resume identity is stable
provisional_features.summary: Delegated-run resume preserves the canonical child identity and normalizes provider-specific compatibility output.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap: Delegated-run resume preserves the canonical child identity and normalizes provider-specific compatibility output.

provisional_features.title: Goal Mode preserves owner boundaries
provisional_features.summary: Goal command identity is catalog-owned while concrete event and persistence semantics remain with the Goal Runtime, contract, and storage owners.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap: Goal command identity is catalog-owned while concrete event and persistence semantics remain with the Goal Runtime, contract, and storage owners.

provisional_features.title: Web intent mappings propagate to all named callers
provisional_features.summary: All enumerated GUI, assistant, subagent, Goal Runtime, PRD Builder, and Planning Wizard callers share one dispatcher mapping.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gap: All enumerated GUI, assistant, subagent, Goal Runtime, PRD Builder, and Planning Wizard callers share one dispatcher mapping.

provisional_features.title: Goal command, event, and lifecycle wiring
provisional_features.summary: Goal start and update command identities, catalog registration, event and payload bindings, durable lifecycle transitions, authorization, concurrency, receipts, failure, recovery, and end-to-end wiring closure.
provisional_features.gap_summary: deferred_goal_runtime_event_and_wiring_contracts: UCC-096 registers Goal commands while explicitly declining concrete Goal event payload schemas and leaves command-catalog wiring review future-facing; this window does not provide the result, failure, cancellation, stale-goal, concurrent-update, offline, or accessibility contracts needed to prove Goal start/update behavior end to end. | Observed gaps or unknowns: Goal commands defer their concrete event and payload schema without a precise binding; Goal command IDs are stable but dispatch lifecycle is incomplete; Goal start is receipt-only despite creating lifecycle state.

provisional_features.title: Concern assignment and lifecycle
provisional_features.summary: Concern create, assign, link-evidence, promote, reopen, resolve, and update with legal states, payloads, authority, versions, idempotency, events, projections, and rollback.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Observed gaps or unknowns: Concern events are named but not semantically sufficient; Concern lifecycle events lack a legal transition model.

provisional_features.title: Runtime replan
provisional_features.summary: Runtime replan is a distinct catalog concept because its lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure modes differ from adjacent controls. The replan row names goal.replanned but does not specify source revision preconditions, event payload identity, concurrent replan resolution, downstream propagation completion, partial failure, or rollback.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Preserved gaps, unknowns, or contradictions: Replan lacks version, concurrency, and recovery semantics.

provisional_features.title: Skip-node continuation semantics
provisional_features.summary: Skip-node continuation semantics is a distinct catalog concept because its lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure modes differ from adjacent controls. The Skip Node control emits goal_run.stopped, with no node-skipped event, continuation rule, skipped-node projection, or explicit statement that skipping intentionally terminates the whole run.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Preserved gaps, unknowns, or contradictions: Skip Node is wired to whole-run termination.

provisional_features.title: Node Change Budget
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for node-change-budget. Validated observations: Reusable node change budgets: The schema defines and reuses a strict change-budget object. | Change budget is not a destructive-action protocol: Change budgets constrain path and line counts but do not require disjoint allow/deny sets or destructive-action safeguards.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Change budget is not a destructive-action protocol.

provisional_features.title: Node Execution Ordering
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for node-execution-ordering. Validated observations: Concurrent node claims and writes are unguarded: Node status is represented as a scalar value with no concurrency or transition-authorship metadata. | Example-node behavior is undefined: The optional example boolean has no defined behavioral effect. | Declared deterministic execution ordering: The graph publishes fixed execution-ordering rule labels for readiness, selection, completion, and spec-lock sourcing. | Unknown node fields are explicitly rejected: Node objects are closed against unlisted properties. | Operational ownership and consumers are unspecified: Node shape names objectives and tools but contains no owner, caller, consumer, approver, support, or observability contract. | GUI wording lacks accessibility and localization bindings: The one GUI wording rule has no localization key, assistive semantics, freshness indicator, or broader misleading-state contract. | Status-to-verifier consistency guard: The allowed status states are enumerated and conditionally bound to verifier outcomes. | Node contract and artifact bindings: Every node requires contract_refs, inputs, and outputs, and each input or output entry requires kind and ref.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Concurrent node claims and writes are unguarded; Example-node behavior is undefined; Operational ownership and consumers are unspecified; GUI wording lacks accessibility and localization bindings. Explicit non-gaps: Unknown node fields are explicitly rejected.

provisional_features.title: NodeSeed WorkGraph WorkNode
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for nodeseed-workgraph-worknode. Validated observations: Approval can occur without executable acceptance content: NodeSeed and WorkNode lifecycle statuses are not conditioned on non-empty executable inputs, acceptance criteria, or validators. | NodeSeed review outcome fields can contradict each other: node_seed_review does not bind review_status to decision or require required_changes for a changes-required outcome.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Approval can occur without executable acceptance content; NodeSeed review outcome fields can contradict each other.

provisional_features.title: Plan Node Acceptance Execution
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for plan-node-acceptance-execution. Validated observations: Execution and governance payload is concretely typed: The property contract supplies typed structures for objectives, ProjectContract references, executable acceptance checks, evidence, tool and workspace authority, change budgets, graph links, lifecycle status, verifier results, decisions, and spec-lock requirements. | Acceptance command safety is outside the schema: Acceptance commands are arbitrary non-empty strings with optional cwd and timeout, but the schema does not bind their execution semantics or require safe handling as untrusted input. | Assigned schema source is structurally complete: The schema closes after its reusable acceptance-check and command-spec definitions, and no trailing source content is omitted from the assigned window.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Acceptance command safety is outside the schema. Explicit non-gaps: Assigned schema source is structurally complete.

provisional_features.title: Plan Node Dependency Graph
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for plan-node-dependency-graph. Validated observations: Dependency graph integrity requires an external oracle: Dependency-like fields are non-empty unique string arrays, but this per-node schema provides no referential-integrity, acyclicity, reciprocal-edge, or consistency contract across nodes.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Dependency graph integrity requires an external oracle.

provisional_features.title: Plan Node Lifecycle
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for plan-node-lifecycle. Validated observations: Lifecycle ordering and race semantics are unspecified: The schema constrains each status snapshot but defines no legal prior-to-next transition graph, transition authority, compare-and-swap rule, or concurrency behavior. | Status is coupled to verifier outcome: Conditional branches enforce status-to-verifier-result consistency for terminal, failed, and active statuses, including timestamps for verified, done, and failed nodes. | Failed nodes lack mandatory recovery evidence: Failure snapshots require fail and timestamp through allOf, but verifier_result.message is optional and no structured recovery or rollback data is defined.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Lifecycle ordering and race semantics are unspecified; Failed nodes lack mandatory recovery evidence.

provisional_features.title: Plan Node Requirement Traceability
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for plan-node-requirement-traceability. Validated observations: Requirement traceability is optional: The schema describes requirement_refs as authoritative but does not include it in the root required list and imposes no minimum item count when it is present.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Requirement traceability is optional.

provisional_features.title: Project Plan Node Schema
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for project-plan-node-schema. Validated observations: Closed root node contract: The schema identifies a closed root object and explicitly requires the core node, acceptance, evidence, tool-policy, change-budget, dependency, status, verification, decision, and spec-lock fields.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Explicit non-gaps: Closed root node contract.

provisional_features.title: WorkNode And Executor Activation
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for worknode-and-executor-activation. Validated observations: Activation state list is not a state machine: The activation states array has a minimum of six enum-valued entries but no uniqueness, completeness, ordering, legal-transition, rollback, or concurrency relation. | WorkNode runtime requires attempt governance: The WorkNode runtime requires at least four record contracts plus cardinality and attempt rule lists. | Activation defines a six-state vocabulary: Executor activation declares six allowed state names from activation_pending through active or cancelled_before_mutation and requires records plus transaction rules.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: Activation state list is not a state machine.

provisional_features.title: WorkNode Runtime State Machine
provisional_features.summary: Normalized local concept for worknode-runtime-state-machine. Validated observations: WorkNode invalid-transition rule has no state machine: WorkNode transition receipts carry from_state and to_state and promise to block invalid transitions, but the allowed WorkNode lifecycle states and transition graph are absent from this contract.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Validated gaps or unknowns: WorkNode invalid-transition rule has no state machine.

provisional_features.title: Goal Runtime Events and Certification Receipts
provisional_features.summary: Persists append-only goal revisions and linked GoalRun, verification, WorkNode, completion, evidence, and certification receipts.
provisional_features.gap_summary: Goal revision CAS recovery is not operationally defined; Receipt-chain persistence lacks atomic chain and retention rules; Goal certification can be accepted without positive evidence

Kept distinct because it is retired migration lineage with no live product-coverage authority.
Kept distinct because it concerns atomic snapshot identity across buildability and readiness inputs.
Kept distinct because it is the user-visible accessibility contract for the Open Folder control.
Kept distinct because it preserves delegated child task identity across resume, not Goal lifecycle identity.
Kept distinct because it defines command-catalog ownership boundaries while deferring concrete Goal Runtime semantics.
Kept distinct because it propagates web intent dispatcher mappings to named callers.
Merged because both members describe the same Goal start/update command, event, lifecycle, and end-to-end wiring closure under the same Goal Runtime and command-wiring authority.
Merged because both members describe the same Goal start/update command, event, lifecycle, and end-to-end wiring closure under the same Goal Runtime and command-wiring authority.

Kept distinct because it governs deterministic graph execution ordering, claims, writes, and node selection.
Kept distinct because it models NodeSeed review, WorkGraph, and WorkNode handoff acceptance rather than runtime transition execution.

relationships.rationale: Executor activation contracts must remain non-executable until the explicit runtime-enablement boundary changes.
Provider-hook and model-transition seams affect Goal lifecycle wiring and receipt attribution without being the same feature.
The design-only plans-to-code handoff names future node artifacts while NodeSeed and WorkGraph contracts define their review and acceptance shapes.
Machine-fixed zero runtime-artifact counts prohibit activation artifacts in the current non-executable governance phase.
Stable catalog command identity interacts with, but does not own, concrete Goal event, persistence, and lifecycle semantics.
End-to-end Goal lifecycle wiring depends on durable revision, receipt-chain, evidence, and certification persistence.
Runtime replanning extends the Goal lifecycle with separate revision, concurrency, propagation, partial-failure, and rollback semantics.
Skip Node promises node-level continuation while the current wiring emits whole-run termination; the WorkNode transition model must resolve that tension.
Execution ordering and concurrent claims consume Plan Node lifecycle status, but ordering and lifecycle remain separate contracts.
Reviewed NodeSeeds and WorkNodes feed later executor activation while retaining separate review and runtime authorities.
Executable acceptance and command-safety rules are a distinct facet of the closed Project Plan Node schema.
Dependency graph integrity extends the per-node root schema with cross-node referential and cycle rules.
Plan Node lifecycle transitions and recovery extend the root node snapshot schema.
Requirement traceability is a distinct root-schema facet whose optionality requires its own closure.
Executor activation and WorkNode runtime transitions interact but have different state vocabularies, records, and failure boundaries.
